rationale: Correct Duke Energy Florida in place. Brookfield's first subscription closed on March 3, 2026, giving Brookfield a 9.19% indirect non-controlling interest through Florida Progress, LLC, while Duke retained 90.81% and operating control. The existing BISS attribution is unsupported; the executed agreement identifies Brookfield Super-Core Infrastructure Partners and Peninsula Power Holdings L.P. Signed follow-on subscriptions remain pending toward a maximum 19.7% interest, so they are recorded separately and are not treated as closed ownership. Florida Progress is the transaction holdco and issuer, not a separate operating PortCo. Direct-party and SEC sources reviewed through August 19, 2026 did not identify a later closing or exit. The 1899 founding field records the operating utility lineage rather than the current LLC's undisclosed formation date.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Duke Energy Florida, LLC is a regulated electric utility providing generation, transmission, distribution and retail power service to about two million residential, commercial and industrial customers across approximately 13,000 square miles in central and western Florida. Its operating utility lineage dates to 1899. Brookfield's first subscription closed on March 3, 2026 through Peninsula Power Holdings L.P., giving Brookfield a 9.19% indirect non-controlling interest through Duke Energy Florida's parent, Florida Progress, LLC; Duke retained 90.81% and operating control. Additional signed subscriptions may increase Brookfield's interest to as much as 19.7%, but no later closing was verified through August 19, 2026. Florida Progress is treated as the transaction holdco rather than a separate PortCo. The current LLC's formation year and Brookfield's allocation among individual BSIP commitment entities are not publicly disclosed.
